name: Pool sizing PgBouncer session lifecycle
short_definition: How Python services size and lifecycle Postgres connections under concurrency: SQLAlchemy AsyncAdaptedQueuePool (pool_size/max_overflow/pool_pre_ping/pool_recycle), when to use NullPool behind PgBouncer/Supabase transaction pooler, asyncpg prepared-statement pitfalls (statement_cache_size / unique prepared_statement_name_func), and tying engine dispose to ASGI lifespan so k8s churn does not leak backends.
scope_in: SQLAlchemy pool_size, max_overflow, pool_timeout, pool_recycle, pool_pre_ping, use_lifo
NullPool vs QueuePool with external poolers
PgBouncer session vs transaction vs statement modes
Session/request lifecycle relative to pool checkout
scope_out: PgBouncer install/ops on bare metal beyond mode semantics

defaults.direct_postgres: create_async_engine(..., pool_size=5, max_overflow=10, pool_pre_ping=True, pool_recycle=1800) as starting point; tune from metrics
defaults.behind_transaction_pgbouncer: poolclass=NullPool + connect_args disabling/renaming prepared statement cache; let pooler multiplex
defaults.supabase_stationary: Prefer direct DB URL :5432 for long-lived single-instance services when connection budget allows
defaults.supabase_autoscaling: Transaction pooler :6543 with asyncpg prepared-statement mitigations; keep client-side pool tiny or NullPool
defaults.lifecycle: One engine per process; create at startup; await dispose() on shutdown; no engine in import-time side effects for tests without fixtures
defaults.budget_rule: workers × (pool_size + max_overflow) + siblings < Postgres max_connections and pooler limits; leave headroom for migrations/admin

use_app_pool_when: Direct connection to Postgres (no transaction pooler)
Session-mode pooler that preserves prepared statements
Stable worker count, need checkout latency wins from warm pool
use_nullpool_or_tiny_pool_when: Risk of connection stampede on cold scale-out
do_not: Do not double-pool aggressively (large SQLAlchemy pool + transaction PgBouncer + many workers)
Do not use default asyncpg prepared statement names unchanged through transaction pooler

do: pool_pre_ping=True for idle disconnects (cloud LB timeouts)
pool_recycle under cloud idle limits (e.g. 15–30 min)
For transaction PgBouncer: NullPool + prepared_statement_name_func uuid OR statement_cache_size=0 / prepared_statement_cache_size=0 per SQLAlchemy+asyncpg guidance
Close/return sessions promptly so connections return to pool
Ready probe: checkout + SELECT 1 with timeout; live probe: no pool required
dont: Don't set pool_size=50 on 4 uvicorn workers blindly (200+ backends)
Don't hold sessions for entire long SSE/LLM streams unless required
Don't ignore DuplicatePreparedStatementError — fix pooler mode/config
Don't use session-level features (LISTEN, temp tables, prepared across txs) on transaction pooler
Don't forget dispose after fork (gunicorn workers need per-worker engine)

code_skeleton:
from uuid import uuid4
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker, create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool

# --- Direct Postgres (long-lived service) ---
engine_direct = create_async_engine(
    "postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@db:5432/app",
    pool_size=5,
    max_overflow=10,
    pool_timeout=30,
    pool_pre_ping=True,
    pool_recycle=1800,
)

# --- Transaction PgBouncer / Supabase :6543 ---
engine_pooler = create_async_engine(
    "postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@pooler:6543/app",
    poolclass=NullPool,
    connect_args={
        # SQLAlchemy official pattern: unique prepared statement names
        "prepared_statement_name_func": lambda: f"__asyncpg_{uuid4()}__",
        # Also commonly set when cache still causes issues:
        "statement_cache_size": 0,
        "prepared_statement_cache_size": 0,
    },
)

SessionLocal = async_sessionmaker(engine_direct, expire_on_commit=False, class_=AsyncSession)

# Lifespan:
# startup: engine ready (lazy connect) / optional warm
# shutdown: await engine.dispose()

async def readiness_check() -> bool:
    async with engine_direct.connect() as conn:
        await conn.exec_driver_sql("SELECT 1")
    return True
failure_modes: Too many clients / remaining connection slots reserved — under-sized Postgres or over-sized app pools
Pool timeout 30s under load → 500s while DB is fine
DuplicatePreparedStatementError / prepared statement does not exist with transaction PgBouncer
Connection leak from sessions not closed on cancel
Scale-out stampede: N new pods × max pool open at once
SSL/idle disconnect without pre_ping → mysterious first-request failures
LISTEN/NOTIFY or advisory locks broken across transaction pooler
anti_patterns: Copy-paste pool_size=20 from blog without worker math
Using Supabase transaction pooler URL with default asyncpg caches
Long transactions spanning external HTTP calls while holding pool checkout
Sharing one engine across forked workers without dispose/recreate
Health liveness that acquires pool connections
Agent defaulting all envs to :6543 without prepared-statement fix

deprecation_watch: Assuming port 6543 is always safe with asyncpg defaults
NullPool on direct DB for high-QPS (extra handshake cost) without reason
QueuePool defaults (5+10) blindly on serverless with 100 instances
ts_boundary: Next.js Supabase clients use HTTP PostgREST — not Postgres connection pools. Python services that open real PG connections must not assume unlimited pool; coordinate max connections with other runtimes (Edge Functions, Rust).
rust_boundary: sqlx/deadpool pools need the same budget math. Prefer one service tier owning heavy pool usage. Rust can hold more efficient pools — still count against Postgres.
supabase_boundary: Supabase: direct vs pooler choice is critical. Transaction pooler incompatible with session features and painful for asyncpg prepared statements. RLS still applies to non-superuser roles; pooler does not replace authz. Prefer service role only server-side. See backend-database.md for RLS; this item is about TCP/session mechanics.
boundary_contracts: Ready probe contract uses short timeout
No LISTEN/long session features on transaction pooler URLs

decision_matrix_row.python: SQLAlchemy pool or NullPool+PgBouncer with asyncpg mitigations
decision_matrix_row.ts: No server pool for typical Next+Supabase HTTP; Edge limits separate
decision_matrix_row.rust: deadpool/sqlx pool with shared connection budget

threats: Connection exhaustion DoS (self-inflicted scale or attacker-triggered work)
Credential leak in connection strings / logs
Noisy neighbor on shared Supabase compute via runaway pools
Session fixation of role/search_path if pool reuses connections without reset
mitigations: Hard caps on pool and worker counts; load-test
Secrets manager; redact URLs in telemetry
pool_reset_on_return / DISCARD ALL at pooler; avoid setting session GUCs without reset
Rate limit expensive endpoints that hold DB work
